newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's unsecured bank loans rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's unsecured bank loans rise in 1996.

text.p: The ratio of unsecured loans by South Korea's commercial banks to their total loans rose to 61.9 percent at the end of 1996, up from 55.8 percent a year earlier, the Office of Bank Supervision said on Tuesday.
A statement said the portion of bank loans secured with collateral fell to 32 percent from 37.6 percent.

Unsecured loans included those with repayment guarantees from legal bodies, those with multiple partial guarantees and purely unsecured ones. Total loans extended by the nation's commercial banks -- 15 nationwide banks and 10 regional banks -- stood at 114.7 trillion won at the end of last year.
The office said loans guaranteed by trust guarantee funds, the government and financial institutions accounted for 6.1 percent, down from 6.6 percent.
Kookmin Bank topped the list of both unsecured loans and those secured by collateral with 6.71 trillion won and 7.97 trillion won.
